finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id never enforces ownership. Any authenticated non-admin user can delete any project.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled path param req.params.id, with any authenticated req.user that is not an admin.
finding.sink: api.js:19 req.store.projects.delete(project.id), a destructive write on another user's resource.

trace.note: project loaded by attacker-supplied id with no ownership filter
authorized() is a pure predicate that returns a boolean and never throws
return value of authorized(req.user, project) is discarded, so the check has no effect

finding.guards_checked: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean and does not throw, so the call at line 18 is a no-op. authorize() at api.js:4-10 would throw 403, but this route calls the wrong helper. No other guard is visible in this file. Route-level middleware is out of scope and could not be checked.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. authorized() at api.js:12-14 is a pure boolean predicate, and its result at api.js:18 is discarded as a bare statement, so it blocks nothing. authorize() (api.js:4-10, throws 403) exists but is not called on the DELETE route. The only other file in the directory is .claude/skills/... markdown, so no route-level ownership middleware is visible.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: project is loaded by attacker-supplied id at api.js:17 with no ownership filter, the boolean from authorized() at api.js:18 is discarded, and api.js:19 deletes the project for any authenticated non-admin caller. The attacker is an authenticated low-privilege user, a role that does not already hold this power, and no effective guard exists in the code available.

finding.claim: authorize() and authorized() disagree on admin checks and on undefined owners, and both throw TypeError on a missing project. This creates a conditional authorization bypass and an existence oracle.
finding.source: req.user shape (no id, or a truthy non-boolean isAdmin) and req.params.id for a nonexistent project.
finding.sink: Authorization decision at api.js:5 (authorize) and api.js:13 (authorized). Missing-project path at api.js:17-18 and 24-25.

trace.note: authorize() grants admin on any truthy isAdmin via !user.isAdmin
authorized() grants admin only on strict isAdmin === true
if resource.ownerId and user.id are both undefined, the !== test is false and access is granted
for a nonexistent id, project is undefined and line 18 or 25 throws TypeError (500), not 404

finding.guards_checked: authorize() at line 5 blocks a non-owner without isAdmin. The undefined-owner bypass requires req.user.id to be undefined while project ownerId is also undefined, which is reachable only if upstream auth sets req.user without an id. The admin inconsistency matters only if isAdmin can arrive as a non-boolean truthy value from an attacker-controlled source, which this file does not show.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. On the DELETE route, api.js:18 calls authorized(req.user, project) as a bare statement and discards its boolean return, so api.js:19 deletes the project regardless of the result. On the PUT route, authorize() (api.js:5-9) is a throwing guard and does block non-owners without a truthy isAdmin. The undefined-owner path at api.js:5 and the isAdmin inconsistency at api.js:5 vs api.js:13 are real but are not needed for the main bypass.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code (api.js:5, 13, 17-18, 24-25), and the DELETE handler at api.js:18-19 discards authorized()'s return value, so any authenticated user can delete any project; a nonexistent id gives a 500 TypeError while an existing one gives 204, which is also an existence oracle. The candidate understates this by framing it as a conditional bypass that needs undefined owners, so the real issue is broader and unconditional on that route, assuming upstream auth sets req.user for any logged-in user.
